_readme: Monthly digest content for the Tax Research Updates section. Add each new development as an item with a "month" field ("August 2026" or "2026-08"). The page shows a rolling 3-month window computed at page load, newest first, so older items drop off on their own. Refresh each category's "overview" when you publish. "summary" and "overview" accept inline HTML such as links; "title" and "firms" are escaped.
source: Synthesized from Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG, Grant Thornton and RSM client alerts.

State Income Tax.overview: State income tax activity in early 2025 has been defined by aggressive apportionment rule changes, continued fallout from remote work policies, and several states revisiting pass-through entity tax elections. Deloitte, EY, and KPMG have all urged multistate businesses to reassess filing positions before Q2 estimated payments.

items.title: Massachusetts Updates Apportionment Rules for Financial Institutions
items.summary: Massachusetts finalized revised apportionment regulations under 830 CMR 63.38.1 affecting banks and financial services firms with in-state activity. The rules revise receipts factor sourcing for interest income and loan origination fees, potentially increasing Massachusetts taxable income for many out-of-state lenders. Deloitte and PwC issued client alerts recommending immediate review of apportionment computations for tax years 2022 forward, as the rules apply retroactively. Companies with Massachusetts nexus should model the impact before the April 2025 extension deadline.

items.title: New York Releases Guidance on Remote Worker Convenience Rule
items.summary: The New York Department of Taxation and Finance released TSB-M-25(1)I clarifying the convenience-of-the-employer rule for hybrid workers post-pandemic. The guidance confirms that days worked remotely for the employee's convenience remain sourced to New York, maintaining one of the nation's most aggressive remote work tax positions. EY and Grant Thornton flagged significant exposure for multistate employers who assumed pandemic-era flexibility would persist. Employers should audit payroll withholding and employee nexus determinations for 2024 and 2025 tax years.

items.title: Illinois Enacts PTE Tax Expansion, Aligns Rate to 4.95%
items.summary: Illinois SB 1814 expanded eligibility for the state's pass-through entity tax election and aligned the PTE rate with the individual income tax rate of 4.95%, effective for tax years beginning January 1, 2025. KPMG and RSM noted the election deadline is the original return due date with no extension available, making timely action critical. Partnerships with tiered structures should evaluate whether each entity layer should make the election independently. The change provides meaningful SALT cap relief for owners of S corporations and partnerships with Illinois operations.

items.title: California FTB Issues Market-Based Sourcing Guidance for Services
items.summary: The California Franchise Tax Board issued FTB Notice 2025-02 providing updated market-based sourcing guidance for service receipts under CRTC §25136, particularly for technology and consulting firms. The notice clarifies the hierarchy of sourcing methods and introduces new examples for subscription-based software and professional service engagements. Deloitte and EY highlighted that companies relying on cost-of-performance sourcing for California may face audit exposure for open years. Affected taxpayers should consider protective refund claims while reviewing their sourcing methodology.

items.title: Ohio CAT Expansion Increases Filing Obligations for Remote Sellers
items.summary: Ohio's Commercial Activity Tax annual minimum tax thresholds were revised under HB 96, with the taxable gross receipts exclusion reduced from $150,000 to $100,000, drawing more businesses into the CAT filing regime. Grant Thornton and RSM both flagged the change as particularly impactful for service businesses with Ohio customers previously below the threshold. The change is effective for 2025 annual periods and quarterly filings. Businesses should reassess their Ohio CAT registration and payment obligations immediately.

items.title: Georgia Reduces Corporate Income Tax Rate to 5.39% for 2025
items.summary: Georgia's automatic income tax rate reduction mechanism triggered a cut in the corporate income tax rate from 5.49% to 5.39% effective January 1, 2025, pursuant to the revenue surplus provisions of HB 1437. PwC and KPMG noted implications for deferred tax asset and liability remeasurement under ASC 740. Public companies with significant Georgia operations should evaluate the financial statement impact for Q1 2025 reporting. The rate reduction also affects PTE tax elections made at the entity level for Georgia purposes.

Sales & Use Tax.overview: Sales and use tax complexity continued to accelerate in early 2025, driven by expanding digital services taxation, aggressive enforcement of economic nexus thresholds, and new marketplace facilitator liability rules. RSM and Deloitte have flagged that audit activity by state revenue departments is at a multi-year high, particularly targeting software-as-a-service and digital product sellers.

items.title: Texas Comptroller Issues SaaS Taxability Ruling Affecting Cloud Vendors
items.summary: The Texas Comptroller issued Policy Letter Ruling No. 2025-001 concluding that most SaaS arrangements constitute taxable data processing services subject to Texas sales tax at 80% of the sales price. The ruling reversed several prior private letter rulings that had treated certain SaaS products as nontaxable information services. Deloitte and RSM issued immediate alerts urging SaaS vendors with Texas customers to evaluate their product classification and billing systems. Companies that have not been collecting Texas tax on SaaS revenue face substantial back-tax exposure and should consider a voluntary disclosure filing.

items.title: Illinois Expands Marketplace Facilitator Rules to Cover Service Platforms
items.summary: Illinois enacted SB 2024 extending marketplace facilitator collection and remittance obligations to platforms that facilitate the sale of services, effective July 1, 2025. The expansion covers platforms connecting buyers and sellers of repair services, personal services, and certain professional services. KPMG and Grant Thornton flagged significant compliance challenges for platforms that have not built tax collection infrastructure for service transactions. Affected platforms should begin system updates immediately given the July effective date.

items.title: Washington State Clarifies B&O Tax Treatment of Digital Advertising
items.summary: The Washington Department of Revenue issued Excise Tax Advisory ETA 3215.2025 addressing the Business & Occupation tax classification of digital advertising services sold by out-of-state vendors to Washington customers. The advisory applies the service-and-other-activities B&O tax rate of 1.5% and adopts market-based sourcing for apportioning gross receipts to Washington. EY and PwC noted the guidance affects all companies monetizing digital ad inventory through Washington-based publishers or audiences. Businesses should review their Washington B&O tax filing positions and prior-year apportionment calculations.

items.title: New York Addresses Sales Tax on Bundled Software and Services
items.summary: The New York Tax Appeals Tribunal ruled in In the Matter of Cloudware Solutions LLC that bundled contracts combining taxable software licenses with nontaxable professional services must be unbundled using objective allocation methods, with the burden of proof on the taxpayer. RSM and Deloitte recommended that technology companies review contract structures and invoicing practices to ensure defensible service/software separation. Companies relying on lump-sum billing for mixed contracts face the greatest audit risk. The decision raises the evidentiary standard for allocation significantly.

items.title: Colorado Enacts Retail Delivery Fee Increase Effective July 2025
items.summary: Colorado HB 1004 increased the Retail Delivery Fee from $0.29 to $0.35 per delivery effective July 1, 2025, and expanded the fee to cover deliveries made by marketplace facilitators on behalf of third-party sellers. Grant Thornton and KPMG highlighted that while the fee is customer-facing, the remittance obligation falls on the retailer or marketplace. Businesses should update checkout systems and verify that fee collection workflows are configured for the July effective date. The expansion to marketplace transactions is particularly significant for platforms with third-party seller models.

items.title: Multistate Wayfair Enforcement Sweeps Targeting Remote Sellers
items.summary: Revenue departments in Florida, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania launched coordinated economic nexus enforcement sweeps in Q1 2025, sending notices to remote sellers that crossed nexus thresholds in 2022 or 2023 but never registered. PwC and EY reported the notices are accompanied by assessments covering multiple periods plus penalties and interest, with limited abatement options. Sellers who receive notices should engage tax counsel immediately, as the voluntary disclosure window closes once an audit notice is issued. Businesses that have not audited their economic nexus footprint since 2022 should prioritize doing so.

Nexus & Apportionment.overview: Nexus and apportionment issues in early 2025 are shaped by proliferating factor-presence nexus standards, states updating market-based sourcing rules for intangibles and services, and renewed litigation over constitutional limits of state income tax jurisdiction. KPMG and EY identify throwback rule reform as the single most impactful apportionment issue for multistate manufacturers and distributors.

items.title: Michigan Adopts Market-Based Sourcing for All Business Income
items.summary: Michigan finalized administrative rule R 206.13 adopting market-based sourcing for all business income receipts, replacing the prior cost-of-performance methodology effective for tax years beginning January 1, 2025. The change significantly affects service companies and IP licensors that historically sourced receipts to Michigan based on where services were performed. Deloitte and PwC recommended immediate apportionment impact modeling, particularly for companies with large Michigan-based workforces serving out-of-state clients. Taxpayers may benefit from filing amended returns under the new methodology where the statute of limitations remains open.

items.title: Minnesota Supreme Court Rules on Factor-Presence Nexus for Holding Companies
items.summary: In Apex Holdings LLC v. Commissioner of Revenue, the Minnesota Supreme Court upheld an assessment against an out-of-state holding company with substantial Minnesota-source royalty income but no physical presence, finding the state's factor-presence nexus statute satisfies constitutional due process under the Complete Auto test. The decision creates precedent for Minnesota's aggressive economic nexus posture and may embolden other states. EY and KPMG flagged that IP holding company structures generating royalties from Minnesota licensees should be reviewed immediately. Taxpayers with similar profiles should assess registration, filing, and back-tax exposure.

items.title: Texas Eliminates Throwback Rule for Manufacturers Effective 2025
items.summary: Texas HB 5 eliminated the throwback rule for manufacturers, meaning receipts from sales of goods shipped to purchasers in states where the seller lacks nexus will no longer be thrown back to Texas for franchise tax purposes, effective for reports due on or after January 1, 2025. RSM and Grant Thornton identified this as a major apportionment benefit for Texas-based manufacturers with national distribution. Companies should recompute Texas apportionment and may find significant franchise tax savings. The change also warrants a review of intercompany pricing arrangements structured partly around prior throwback exposure.

items.title: Pennsylvania Issues Guidance on Intangible Income Nexus
items.summary: The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue issued Corporation Tax Bulletin 2025-01 clarifying that out-of-state corporations receiving royalties, interest, or other intangible income from Pennsylvania sources are subject to Pennsylvania CNIT if receipts exceed the $500,000 bright-line economic nexus threshold under Act 90 of 2022. Deloitte and EY noted that many corporate groups have not assessed Pennsylvania nexus for treasury or IP subsidiary entities. Affected entities should evaluate registration obligations and consider voluntary disclosure to limit penalty exposure. The bulletin specifically addresses common IP holding company, intercompany lending, and trademark licensor structures.

items.title: MTC Releases Updated Model Market-Based Sourcing Regulation
items.summary: The Multistate Tax Commission released an updated Model Regulation for Market-Based Sourcing incorporating revised guidance on sourcing receipts from digital services, subscription products, and software licenses. PwC and KPMG noted that several states are expected to adopt the model regulation during 2025 legislative sessions, potentially creating simultaneous sourcing rule changes across multiple jurisdictions. Multistate businesses should monitor their key states' adoption of the MTC model and prepare for potential mid-year effective dates. Companies with customized sourcing methodologies should evaluate whether their positions remain defensible under the updated model.

items.title: New Jersey Expands Combined Reporting to Include Foreign Affiliates
items.summary: New Jersey AB 3816 amended the combined reporting statute to require inclusion of certain foreign affiliates where the affiliate's income is subject to federal Subpart F or GILTI inclusion, effective for privilege periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025. Grant Thornton and RSM identified the change as significantly impacting multinationals with New Jersey operations, potentially increasing the New Jersey tax base substantially. Companies must analyze their global corporate structure to determine which foreign entities must be included in the combined return. Affected taxpayers should model the impact and assess whether water's-edge elections or other planning strategies are warranted.

Tax Credits & Incentives.overview: State tax credit and incentive activity in early 2025 has been dominated by manufacturing reshoring credits, green energy incentive expansions mirroring federal IRA provisions, and significant changes to R&D credit regimes. EY and Grant Thornton have noted that state R&D credit audits are intensifying, with revenue departments scrutinizing qualified research expenditure definitions and contract research cost allocations.

items.title: Georgia Launches $1B Film and Entertainment Tax Credit Expansion
items.summary: Georgia enacted SB 89 expanding the Film Tax Credit program and eliminating the sunset provision, cementing Georgia's position as the top film production state nationally. The credit remains at 20% of qualified production expenditures with a 10% uplift for productions including a Georgia promotional logo, and transferability provisions are preserved. EY and Deloitte highlighted that the credit continues to be highly marketable, with secondary markets trading Georgia film credits at approximately 88–92 cents on the dollar. Production companies and credit purchasers should ensure compliance with the updated certification and audit procedures required under the new legislation.

items.title: Federal IRA Credit Transferability Drives State Conformity Questions
items.summary: With IRA transferable and direct-pay clean energy credits now fully operational, states are grappling with whether transferred credits are includible in state taxable income of the buyer or seller. States including California, New York, and Illinois have issued conflicting guidance on conformity with federal exclusion treatment. PwC and KPMG published detailed state-by-state matrices tracking each state's conformity position. Buyers and sellers of federal clean energy tax credits must carefully evaluate state income tax implications at both the transferor and transferee level before completing transactions.

items.title: Texas Launches Semiconductor and Advanced Manufacturing Jobs Credit
items.summary: Texas HB 12 established a new Texas Semiconductor and Advanced Manufacturing Jobs Tax Credit providing $2,500 per qualifying job created at a new advanced manufacturing facility, with enhanced credits of $5,000 per job in designated economic development zones. RSM and Grant Thornton issued planning alerts noting the credit stacks with existing Chapter 313 successor incentives and federal CHIPS Act benefits. Companies planning Texas manufacturing expansions should model the combined state and federal incentive stack before finalizing site selection decisions. The credit is refundable for qualifying startups.

items.title: New York R&D Credit Rules Updated, QRE Definition Tightened
items.summary: The New York Department of Taxation and Finance issued TSB-M-25(2)C revising the definition of qualified research expenditures for the New York Investment Tax Credit's research component, disallowing costs of foreign contract research and certain overhead allocations previously accepted in practice. Deloitte and EY flagged that the change narrows the credit base for companies with offshore R&D components. Taxpayers claiming the New York R&D credit should review QRE computations and prepare for increased audit scrutiny. Amended returns may be warranted for prior years where now-disallowed costs were included.

items.title: Illinois EDGE Credit Program Reopens with Enhanced Manufacturing Incentives
items.summary: Illinois reopened its Economic Development for a Growing Economy credit program under expanded guidelines that increase the maximum credit from 100% to 150% of incremental state income tax withholdings of new hires for qualifying manufacturers and logistics companies. KPMG and PwC noted that EDGE credits are among the most valuable discretionary incentives in the Midwest and have historically been underutilized by smaller companies. The program now includes a fast-track application process for projects creating 100 or more full-time jobs within 24 months. Companies considering Illinois expansions or relocations should engage the Department of Commerce early in the site selection process.

items.title: Missouri Enacts Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credit Increase to $135M Cap
items.summary: Missouri SB 578 increased the Historic Tax Credit cap from $90 million to $135 million annually and streamlined the certification process, effective for applications submitted after July 1, 2025. The credit equals 25% of qualified rehabilitation expenditures for certified historic structures, with credits that are transferable and carry forward 10 years. RSM and Grant Thornton highlighted that the cap increase is expected to significantly reduce the current multi-year waitlist for credit allocations. Real estate developers and investors with Missouri historic rehabilitation projects should assess eligibility and timing relative to the new cap and application procedures.

Audit Defense.overview: State tax audit activity reached a five-year high in early 2025 as revenue departments that paused enforcement during the pandemic fully ramped up examination programs. Digital economy audits, nexus examinations triggered by economic nexus data matching, and transfer pricing scrutiny are the three most prevalent audit categories. States are increasingly using third-party data analytics firms to identify audit targets.

items.title: California FTB Launches Targeted Digital Economy Audit Program
items.summary: The California Franchise Tax Board announced a dedicated Digital Economy Compliance Initiative in March 2025, deploying specialized audit teams to examine technology companies, digital marketplace operators, and subscription service providers with California nexus. The initiative focuses on market-based sourcing compliance, California-source income determination, and treatment of digital advertising revenues. EY and Deloitte noted that FTB exam opening rates for tech-sector companies increased approximately 40% in Q1 2025. Companies that have not recently reviewed their California apportionment methodology should conduct a pre-audit risk assessment.

items.title: New York DTF Issues Subpoenas in Cryptocurrency Income Examinations
items.summary: The New York Department of Taxation and Finance began issuing third-party subpoenas to cryptocurrency exchanges operating in New York to identify taxpayers with unreported cryptocurrency income for tax years 2019–2023. The subpoenas request transaction-level data including wallet addresses, trade histories, and fiat currency conversion records. KPMG and RSM flagged that New York is the first state to pursue crypto income enforcement at this scale, with other states likely to follow through federal-state information sharing. Taxpayers with significant cryptocurrency activity who have not fully reported gains should consult with tax counsel about voluntary disclosure options immediately.

items.title: Texas Comptroller Increases Transfer Pricing Scrutiny for Related-Party Royalties
items.summary: The Texas Comptroller's office issued a policy memorandum directing franchise tax auditors to apply heightened scrutiny to related-party royalty deductions, citing concerns about artificial income shifting through IP holding company structures. Auditors are instructed to require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation meeting IRC §482 standards and to assess arm's-length royalty rates using the comparable uncontrolled royalty method. PwC and Grant Thornton recommended that Texas taxpayers with related-party IP arrangements prepare or update their transfer pricing documentation before the next audit cycle. Companies without contemporaneous documentation face a presumption in favor of the state's proposed adjustments.

items.title: Illinois DOR Issues Guidance on Statute of Limitations Waivers
items.summary: The Illinois Department of Revenue issued General Information Letter IT 25-0003 clarifying circumstances under which the Department will request statute of limitations waivers during income tax examinations, and establishing a new taxpayer right to refuse a waiver request without adverse inference. The guidance establishes maximum waiver extension periods of 12 months per request, with a total cap of 36 months beyond the standard limitations period. Deloitte and EY recommended that taxpayers carefully evaluate the strategic implications of waiver requests before signing, particularly where significant issues are under examination. Taxpayers approached for waivers should engage experienced SALT counsel to assess the risk-benefit tradeoff.

items.title: Pennsylvania Introduces Pre-Audit Compliance Review Program
items.summary: Pennsylvania's Department of Revenue launched a voluntary Pre-Audit Compliance Review program allowing corporate taxpayers to request a pre-exam review of Corporate Net Income Tax returns before a formal audit is initiated, with participation resulting in reduced penalties if issues are identified. The program is available to corporate taxpayers with Pennsylvania CNIT liability exceeding $1 million annually. KPMG and RSM noted the program offers a significant risk management opportunity for companies that have undergone major transactions, restructurings, or apportionment methodology changes in recent years. Applications for the first cohort are due by June 30, 2025.

items.title: MTC Joint Audit Program Reports Record 23 Simultaneous Audits
items.summary: The Multistate Tax Commission's Joint Audit Program initiated a record 23 simultaneous multistate audits in Q1 2025, with participating states including California, New York, Illinois, Texas, and Pennsylvania coordinating examination of large multistate corporations on transfer pricing, intercompany transactions, and apportionment methodology. Grant Thornton and PwC advised that companies under MTC joint audit are subject to information requests from all participating states simultaneously, significantly amplifying compliance burden. Businesses that receive an MTC joint audit notice should immediately assemble a centralized response team and establish a single coordination point across all state jurisdictions.

Voluntary Disclosure.overview: Voluntary disclosure activity remained robust in early 2025, driven by companies catching up on pandemic-era nexus obligations and ongoing expansion of economic nexus enforcement across income, sales, and gross receipts taxes. The MTC's National Nexus Program continues to offer streamlined multistate disclosures, and several states have introduced enhanced penalty waiver programs. RSM and Grant Thornton recommend conducting comprehensive nexus reviews before June 30, 2025 to take advantage of current favorable settlement terms.

items.title: MTC National Nexus Program Updates Lookback Period Policy for 2025
items.summary: The Multistate Tax Commission updated its National Nexus Program guidelines effective January 1, 2025, standardizing the lookback period for income tax voluntary disclosures at three years for all participating states, down from the prior five-year standard in many jurisdictions. The change significantly reduces the financial exposure of voluntary disclosures and is expected to increase participation rates among companies with long-standing undisclosed filing obligations. RSM and Deloitte highlighted the policy change as a rare window of reduced exposure for companies contemplating multistate disclosures. The three-year lookback applies only to prospective disclosures and does not affect companies already under audit.

items.title: Florida Introduces Voluntary Disclosure Incentive Program for Remote Sellers
items.summary: Florida's Department of Revenue launched a limited-duration Voluntary Disclosure Incentive Program through June 30, 2025, offering full penalty waiver and a reduced 2-year lookback for remote sellers with unregistered Florida sales tax obligations arising from economic nexus. The program targets sellers who crossed Florida's $100,000 economic nexus threshold in 2021 or 2022 but never registered. EY and KPMG flagged the program as particularly valuable given Florida's standard 3-year lookback and aggressive penalty regime. E-commerce businesses and marketplace sellers that have not confirmed their Florida registration status should act before the June 30 deadline.

items.title: Texas Comptroller Expands Managed Audit Program to Sales Tax
items.summary: The Texas Comptroller expanded its Managed Audit Program to include sales and use tax, allowing qualifying businesses to self-conduct an audit under Comptroller supervision in exchange for reduced penalties and an agreed 3-year lookback. PwC and Grant Thornton noted that the managed audit option is particularly advantageous for companies with complex product taxability questions or sourcing issues. Businesses should apply before an audit notice is issued to remain eligible for the program. The expansion is particularly timely given increased Texas sales tax enforcement activity in the digital services sector.

items.title: California OTA Clarifies Voluntary Disclosure Criminal Referral Protections
items.summary: California's Office of Tax Appeals issued precedential decision OTA Case No. 23-500214 confirming that information disclosed during the FTB's Voluntary Disclosure Program may not be used as the basis for a criminal tax referral, codifying existing administrative practice into binding precedent. Deloitte and EY noted the decision provides important assurance for taxpayers with significant undisclosed California income tax liabilities deterred by criminal exposure concerns. The decision is consistent with similar protections in most other states but represents an important clarification of California law. Taxpayers with substantial undisclosed California income tax obligations should consult with counsel about the expanded protections and disclosure timing.

items.title: New York Launches Amnesty for Unreported Remote Worker Withholding
items.summary: New York launched a limited amnesty program through August 31, 2025, allowing out-of-state employers to come into compliance with New York payroll withholding obligations for remote employees, with penalties fully waived and interest capped at 50% of the standard rate. The program targets the significant population of employers that hired New York-based remote workers during 2020–2022 without registering for New York withholding. KPMG and RSM identified the amnesty as critical given that New York's standard withholding penalties are substantial and the Department has begun cross-matching W-2 data to identify noncompliant employers. Employers should audit their remote workforce locations and register under the amnesty before the August deadline.

items.title: MTC NexusConnect Platform Streamlines Simultaneous Multistate Disclosures
items.summary: The Multistate Tax Commission's NexusConnect electronic disclosure platform reached full operational capacity in April 2025, allowing taxpayers to file voluntary disclosure agreements simultaneously with up to 38 participating states through a single electronic submission, reducing average processing time from 6 months to approximately 8 weeks. Grant Thornton and PwC published implementation guides noting the platform is particularly valuable for companies with obligations in 10 or more states. Companies planning multistate disclosures should evaluate NexusConnect as the primary filing mechanism and confirm which target states are participating in the current program year. The streamlined process substantially reduces legal and administrative costs compared to separate state negotiations.
